newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran's NIOC to develop Salman Khuff field - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iran's NIOC to develop Salman Khuff field - MEES.

text.p: The National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) has decided to develop the Salman Khuff gas field on its own due to little foreign interest in the project, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) newsletter reported on Monday.
"In view of the apparent lack of international interest in Salman, NIOC has now decided to develop the field on its own," MEES said.
"The timing of this decision was no doubt influenced by recently-mooted plans on the part of Abu Dhabi to double gas production capacity at ABK to 640 million cfd," it added.
Part of the Salman field is in Abu Dhabi waters, where it is known as the Abu Al Bukhoosh (ABK) field.
Salman is one of many offshore oil and gas structures which Iran has offered to foreign contractors.

"But potential investors have so far been deterred by the relative low condensate content of its gas reserves as well as the lack of ready outlets for the 500 million cfd or so of gas which is slated to be produced from the project," MEES said.
The newsletter said NIOC plans for Salman field included a four-year development schedule to produce at least 500 million cfd of gas plus liquids.
MEES said total field development costs are estimated by NIOC at $400-500 million.

News of NIOC's Salman Khuff plans comes after Iran last month awarded the state-owned Iranian Offshore Engineering Construction Co the contract to develop the offshore Soroush field. Soroush was also originally offered to foreign investors.
